core_obligations: Reduce to the case where no prime contains another and order the primes so that x lies outside the first s - 1 and inside the remaining ones (proof lines 2823-2825).
If some prime still contains the whole coset, find y in I outside it and f in the intersection of the earlier primes but outside it (proof lines 2826-2827).
Adjust x by adding the product fy and conclude by induction on the number s of primes already avoided (proof lines 2828-2829).
proof_roadmap: Normalise the list of primes and split them by whether they contain x (proof lines 2822-2825).
Move x out of one more prime by adding an element of I and iterate (proof lines 2826-2830).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if the coset x + I is not contained in any of finitely many primes, then there is an element y of I with x + y outside all of them (statement lines 2813-2820). The proof does not use the general prime avoidance lemma in the form it is usually quoted: it removes inclusions among the primes, splits them by whether they contain x, finds an element of I outside the first bad prime together with a multiplier lying in all the earlier primes but not in that one, and adds their product to x, concluding by induction on the number of primes already avoided (proof lines 2822-2830). The construction of the adjusting element is the substance and the author writes out each step. H2.
